title: Days, months, seasons
subtitle: Monday, July, in the summer
summary: Say the days, months and seasons in English, use capital letters correctly, and choose between on Monday, at the weekend and in July.

lesson.heading: How we cut up time
lesson.note: A year with 366 days is a leap year.

lesson.heading: Days of the week
lesson.text: The seven days are **Sunday**, **Monday**, **Tuesday**, **Wednesday**, **Thursday**, **Friday** and **Saturday**. The names of the days always begin with a capital letter in English. Saturday + Sunday = **the weekend**.

examples.text: I'm going to a party on **Saturday**.
Her birthday is on **Thursday** this year.
She wanted to have the party at **the weekend**.

lesson.heading: Yesterday, today, tomorrow
lesson.text: If today is Wednesday, then Tuesday was **yesterday** and Monday was **the day before yesterday**. Thursday is **tomorrow** and Friday is **the day after tomorrow**.

examples.text: Monday between 12 pm and 6 pm = **Monday afternoon**.

lesson.heading: on Monday, at the weekend
lesson.text: We say **on** + a day of the week, but **at** + the weekend.

examples.text: I saw her **on** Friday. / I saw her **on** Tuesday evening.
I went to the cinema **at** the weekend.

lesson.heading: Months and seasons
lesson.text: The twelve months are **January**, **February**, **March**, **April**, **May**, **June**, **July**, **August**, **September**, **October**, **November** and **December**. Months always begin with a capital letter. The four seasons are **spring**, **summer**, **autumn** and **winter** - and they do *not* usually start with a capital letter.

examples.text: I love going to barbecues **in the summer**.
My birthday is **in winter** and it's too cold to eat outside.

lesson.text: Learn this old rhyme: Thirty days has September, April, June and November. All the rest have thirty-one, except for February, which has twenty-eight days and twenty-nine in each leap year.

exercises.explanation: There are 100 years in a century.

exercises.prompt: A year which has 366 days is called ___.
exercises.explanation: A year with 366 days is a leap year.

exercises.prompt: Thirty days has September, April, June and ___.
exercises.explanation: September, April, June and November all have 30 days.

exercises.prompt: These short forms are common in diaries. Match each one with the full word.

exercises.statement: I'm going to a party on saturday for Valentina's birthday.
exercises.explanation: I'm going to a party on Saturday for Valentina's birthday. Days always begin with a capital letter.

exercises.statement: She wanted to have the party in the weekend.
exercises.explanation: She wanted to have the party at the weekend.

exercises.statement: I love going to barbecues on the summer.
exercises.explanation: I love going to barbecues in the summer.
We use in with months and seasons.

exercises.prompt: Is each word a day, a month or a season?
Put the four seasons in order, starting with the one after winter.
exercises.explanation: The seasons go spring, summer, autumn, winter - all with small letters.

exercises.prompt: What is the seventh month of the year?
exercises.explanation: January, February, March, April, May, June, July - July is the seventh month.
Saturday and Sunday together are the weekend.
